## Roles and persistent priorities

- Coordinator: Astra xhigh. Own whole-game direction, shared contracts, dependencies, task ownership and integration.
- Builders, including graphics/lore/UI implementation: Sol6.1 max. Use committed baselines and isolated worktrees with exclusive paths. Only root dispatches; cap four active agents including root.
- Independent feature/milestone acceptance: non-author Astra xhigh and non-author Sol6.1 max on the same frozen revision, plus root inspection.
- Additional experience critic: Claude Opus5.5/high at the end of each stage below, with a detailed implementation consultation for substantive findings and Sol-authored corrections. Model/effort availability must be verified in the live catalog; report limits honestly.
- Preserve richer cel, vehicle-focused survival/exploration, biome/resource/capability integration, recoverable loss, ambiguous coherent lore and the full approximately ten-hour main-story intent. No grind padding or replacement with a short demo.
- High priorities: intuitive controls and motion, meaningful expedition loop, clear menus, purposeful timing and polished atmosphere. Avoid excessive subtitles/subheadings/repeated helper text in routine UI. Preserve accessibility/story captions and essential warnings; use concise context rather than removing useful information.

## Each build/review/correction cycle

1. Root turns accepted direction into a concrete bounded assignment: source, specification, owned paths, shared interfaces, intended player behavior, meaningful checks and actual playable evidence. Commit before creating implementation worktrees. Keep non-overlapping work parallel only where the interfaces are settled.
2. Sol authors return commits and bounded evidence. Root inspects actual artifacts and combined behavior, reconciles interfaces and freezes the candidate. Do not accept a completion message as proof.
3. Run the existing independent Astra/Sol gate. At a stage exit also obtain a fresh Opus5.5/high thorough experience review of the same candidate and complete applicable scope. With root plus three reviewers this fits the four-slot cap. Preserve independent initial returns; do not have reviewers wait on or copy peers.
4. When Opus identifies substantive issues, request detailed implementation advice from its completed context if useful. Use a same-child follow-up only for this design consultation, not an independent review round. Require concrete modules/interfaces/algorithms, before/after actions, concise UI, compatibility, tradeoffs and verification. Record its own task ID. Root reconciles proposals; do not blindly add physics, new gates, or scope changes that contradict the intended game.
5. Sol implements accepted findings. Run affected checks; fresh independent review tasks receive the original brief, prior findings, dispositions, unresolved objections and updated evidence. Fresh Opus re-review verifies affected experience changes. Resolve all blocking defects; record explicit evidence/reason for disagreements or later-scope work. No finding silently vanishes.
6. Record acceptance, integrate the feature branch through its PR as authorized, then continue the next stage. Use completion notifications, not polling/watch loops. Keep the durable state current; do not pause automatically after an advisory report or milestone. Only a real missing owner choice/constraint should interrupt ordinary progress.

Scope verification should stay proportional. No repeated unchanged art/carrier/depletion matrix without a concrete affected concern. Each stage still needs composed ordinary-control evidence, not only local tests or seeded screenshots. Distinguish imported earned continuations, true fresh play and diagnostics. Human enjoyment, duration, real-mouse comfort, audible mix and representative-GPU measurements remain explicit where not observed.
